title: Ultrafaint [C II] Emission in a Redshift = 2 Gravitationally Lensed Metal-poor Dwarf Galaxy
question: Study the neutral and molecular ISM of the strongly lensed z = 1.844 metal-poor dwarf extreme emission-line galaxy SL2S 0217 via [C II] 158-um and CO(2-1) emission to test [C II]-SFR relations and constrain its gas reservoir.

recipe.goal: Calibrate, concatenate, and image ALMA Band 9 [C II] and 160-um continuum data
recipe.method: Manually flag antennas with high Tsys, calibrate using DV07 as reference antenna, concatenate visibilities from both ALMA programmes while discarding C43-6 baselines > 1000 klambda, and create naturally-weighted dirty image cubes and continuum images at full resolution and with 0.5 and 1.0 arcsec Gaussian uv-tapers.
key_parameters: uv cut: <= 1000 klambda for C43-6; weighting: natural; uv tapers: none, 0.5 arcsec, 1.0 arcsec; cube channel widths: 50-500 MHz (25-225 km/s)

recipe.goal: Extract image-plane spectra and derive source-plane [C II], 160-um continuum, and CO(2-1) upper limits
recipe.method: Project circular source-plane apertures of radius R = 1, 2, and 3 kpc centered on the UV-continuum peak into the sky plane using the Cooray et al. (2011) lens model (retaining only the main arc), extract spectra from the dirty cubes, and integrate over 250 MHz (110 km/s) centered at 667.97 GHz to determine upper limits and de-lensed luminosities.
key_parameters: Aperture radius R <= 3 kpc, uv-taper = 1.0 arcsec, bandwidth = 250 MHz (110 km/s) centered at 667.97 GHz
assumptions: Magnification factors mu = 43, 25, and 16 for R = 1, 2, and 3 kpc apertures (main arc contains 95% of total flux); flat LambdaCDM cosmology with Omega_m = 0.315, H_0 = 67.4 km/s/Mpc (D_L = 14460 Mpc); line width 110 km/s.

recipe.goal: Verify [C II] flux constraint in the (u,v) visibility plane
recipe.method: Extract real and imaginary visibilities over a 250 MHz bandwidth (keeping XX and YY separate), estimate noise from per-scan baseline rms, forward-model sky brightness distributions (HST F606W arc and R <= 1, 2, 3 kpc apertures) multiplied by a Gaussian primary beam for total fluxes from 0 to 50 mJy, and compute the log-likelihood PDF of S_[CII].
key_parameters: Total flux grid: 0 to 50 mJy; primary beam FWHM: 9.0 arcsec at 680 GHz; bandwidth: 250 MHz
assumptions: Primary beam response approximated by a Gaussian.

recipe.goal: Model ionized gas [C II] 158-um emission using photoionization modelling
recipe.method: Run MAPPINGS V photoionization models with STARBURST99 ionizing spectra in a 1D plane-parallel geometry to predict [C II] 158 um, C II] 2325 A, and C III] 1909 A line ratios as a function of starburst age, ionization parameter U, and electron density n_e, and combine with observed Keck UV line fluxes to estimate ionized gas [C II] 158 um luminosity.
key_parameters: Z = 0.05 Z_sun, n_e = 10 and 100 cm^-3, starburst age step = 0.5 Myr (0.5-5.0 Myr), log U = -4.0 to -1.5
assumptions: Uniform ISM, 1D plane-parallel geometry, instantaneous starburst with stellar rotation, no PDR contribution.

recipe.goal: Estimate molecular gas mass upper limits from CO(2-1) and [C II]
recipe.method: Convert source-plane CO(2-1) and [C II] luminosity upper limits into molecular gas mass M_H2 upper limits using CO excitation and alpha_CO assumptions and empirical [C II]-to-H2 conversion relations from Madden et al. (2020) and Zanella et al. (2018).
assumptions: Magnification mu = 16; CO line ratio r_2/1 = 0.6; Galactic alpha_CO = 4.4 M_sun/(K km s^-1 pc^2); M_H2(M20) = 132 x L_[CII]^0.97; M_H2(Z18) = 30 x L_[CII].

score_reason: The paper clearly states the ALMA project codes, antenna flags, reference antenna, uv-cutoff (1000 klambda), weighting, uv-tapers, spectral binning, and MAPPINGS V input parameters. However, reproducing the exact aperture photometry requires the external lens model from Cooray et al. (2011) and manual re-calibration of the Band 9 visibilities without full calibration script details.
rediscovery_reason: Both ALMA datasets (2016.1.00142.S and 2016.1.00776.S) are public in the ALMA archive, the flagging and imaging recipe (discarding >1000 klambda baselines, natural weighting, 0.5 and 1.0 arcsec tapers) is specific, and the main results are quantitative rms sensitivities and flux/luminosity upper limits.
